why.title: The idea
why.text: 21.Bxh6!! offers the bishop on h6. Taking it gives White an attack worth more than the bishop.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: 21.Bxh6 puts the bishop on h6 where it can be taken by the g7 pawn. That's a bishop on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the bishop
why.text: 21…gxh6 is met by 22.Qxh6, taking the h6 pawn and threatening Qg5+, winning a knight. Then 23.b4 threatens bxc5, winning a bishop for a pawn. White is still a pawn down, but the attack is worth more: White is clearly better (+1.85).

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the bishop alone and play 21…Nh7. White answers 22.Be3, and the bishop on h6 gets away. Then 24.Bxd4 takes the bishop on d4, and 25.Qxd4 takes the d4 pawn. White ends up two pawns ahead: White is clearly better (+1.56).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 21.Na4, is clearly weaker (+0.96 against +1.56). Black answers 21…Bd4, planting the bishop on the d4 outpost. That would leave White a little better.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 28.Nxf6+!! offers the knight on f6. Taking it gives White the material back and more.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: 28.Nxf6+ puts the knight on f6 where it can be taken by the queen on e7 and the knight on h7. That's a knight on offer.

why.title: If Black takes the knight
why.text: 28…Nxf6 is met by 29.Qg5+. Then 30.Rxf6 takes the knight on f6, and 32.Bg5+ gives check. Material is level and White is winning (+4.58).

why.title: Black's best try
why.text: Black's best is to leave the knight alone and play 28…Kh8. White answers 29.g5, pushing the passed pawn to g5. Then 30.Nxh7 takes the knight on h7, and 31.Rf6 attacks the bishop on e6, which is undefended. White ends up a pawn ahead: White is winning (+4.56).

opening.name: English Opening: King's English Variation, Four Knights Variation, Flexible Line
points: Both sides followed opening theory up to 5.Bd2: 9 moves in all, 5 by White and 4 by Black.
Black left the book with 5…a5. In 86 games from this position, strong players played 5…O-O (79%) or 5…d5 (10%).
The main line goes on 5…O-O 6.g3 Re8.
From here White scored 46% in those games, with 18% drawn.
